messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> team-eng-oncall (HIGH)
incident-bot: Alert: inference-queue-depth (us-west1) > 5000 for 10m. Autoscaler reported insufficient scaling. Link: https://internal.monitoring/redwood/alert/5250004321

pagerduty-bot: Page sent to oncall rotation. Escalation policy: primary -> ops-lead -> eng-sre.

maria.g: oncall here, seeing the spike. Grafana shows desired replicas 120 -> current 48, queue length steady high. Autoscaler logs show nodes requested but many in Provisioning -> NotReady.

kevin_l: ack. grabbing cluster events now. Can someone confirm pagerduty ack?

pagerduty-bot: Alert acknowledged by kevin_l.

samir: looking at kube events: recently provisioned nodes stuck in NotReady with kubelet failing to start. Errors: "Failed to start kubelet: mount failed: permission denied" repeated. New nodes not joining the cluster, so HPA can't place pods.

ops_lead_jan: Provider console shows instance-init timeout on multiple VMs in the pool. Image pulls were slow and some cloud-init steps timed out. We rolled base image v2.4 earlier today — could be related.

maria.g: run: kubectl get nodes -o wide -> many nodes in status NotReady, age 2-6m. kubectl describe node <id> shows kubelet crashloop. Autoscaler controller log snippet: "scaleUp: requested 24 nodes, waiting for nodes to be ready (timeout)"

kevin_l: I'm going to trigger a manual nodepool scale while we investigate. Creating +10 warm nodes from console to get capacity quickly.

samir: manual resize issued. Also starting a separate nodepool with older image (base-v2.3) as a quick workaround — will label it 'rollout-quick-v2-3'.

maria.g: trying short-term pod-level workaround: patch critical deployments to tolerate potential taints and prefer new nodepool. Not great but should let scheduler place pods sooner. Example patch I ran: 
```
kubectl patch deploy inference-critical -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"nodepool":"rollout-quick-v2-3"}}}}}'
```

ops_lead_jan: Customer impact: increased 5xx rate (502/503) went from 0.2% baseline to ~8% in the last 20m. Latency tail 95p jumped >5s. Noting enterprise customers SlateApps and FinLedger saw retries/timeouts. Escalating to P1. CS notified.

kevin_l: CS and growth pinged. Also adding a temporary routing rule to drop non-critical low-priority batches to conserve capacity.

samir: new nodepool nodes are coming up but entering NotReady initially; however ones spun with base-v2.3 are registering healthy. Starting cordon/drain on a few failing nodes once replacement is stable.

maria.g: queue depth trending: 5200 -> 1600 after manual node additions and patching. Good signal. Latency down to ~1.2s p95 from 5s but still above normal.

ops_lead_jan: work plan / runbook notes: 1) stabilize with v2.3 nodepool, 2) rollback base-image v2.4 for node autoscaling, 3) add healthcheck gating on image promotion, 4) add alert for "node-init-failures" to catch this earlier.

kevin_l: I'm going to leave the console resize in place and open a PR to pin image to v2.3 for autoscaling pools. Will also add a quickscript to detect kubelet mount perms.

samir: temporary mitigation complete: evicted pending pods scheduled onto v2.3 pool, pods came up. Queue now 900. Tracker: https://internal.tools/ops/incidents/5250004321

maria.g: pinging next oncall - @next_oncall_lee you'll take handoff in ~40m. Planning to keep watch for 60m post-normalization and then rollback autoscaler config.

ops_lead_jan: customers notified with brief: "We've identified and mitigated a capacity provisioning issue affecting inference requests in us-west1, mitigation in progress. We will follow up with root cause and remediation."

kevin_l: action items assigned in the incident doc: - PR to pin autoscaler image (kevin_l) - Add node-init-failure alert (maria.g) - Runbook for image promotion gating (samir) - CS follow-up message (ops_lead_jan). ETA to fully recovered: ~25m from now.

maria.g: monitoring: p95 back to 0.35s, error rate down to 0.4%. Queue steady at ~200. Keeping an eye on any resurrection of NotReady nodes.

pagerduty-bot: Alert resolved automatically: queue depth normalized below threshold.

kevin_l: marking incident as mitigated. Will remain on call to confirm stability, then handoff to @next_oncall_lee.

next_oncall_lee: thanks - I'll take over watch. Please leave the runbook and notes in the incident doc and ping if anything flares.

maria.g: saved runbook and added troubleshooting snippets + logs. Closing this thread for the immediate surge. Follow-up RCA scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 PST. :thumbsup:
